question: Neither the manager nor the assistants ___ available today.
solution: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject; assistants is plural, so are is correct.

question: The quality of these products ___ improved considerably.
solution: The subject quality is singular, so has is correct.

question: A number of applicants ___ requested additional information.
solution: A number of means several, so it takes a plural verb.

question: Each of the proposals ___ carefully examined before approval.
solution: Each is singular and therefore takes was.

question: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk in the heat.
solution: A distance treated as one unit takes a singular verb.

question: The committee, together with its chairperson, ___ meeting tomorrow.
solution: The main subject committee is singular; together with does not change the number.

question: By the time the guests arrived, we ___ dinner.
solution: The earlier completed action takes the past perfect.

question: She ___ in Kathmandu since 2022.
solution: Since a point in the past with continuing relevance normally takes the present perfect.

question: When I reached the office, the meeting ___.
solution: The meeting started before I reached the office, so past perfect is appropriate.

question: This time next month, they ___ the new bridge.
solution: A completed action expected before a future point takes the future perfect.

question: The new policy aims to reduce costs, improve service and ___.
solution: The three coordinated verbs should be parallel: reduce, improve, increase.

question: The officer is responsible for planning, budgeting and ___.
solution: The preposition for is followed by parallel gerunds: planning, budgeting, supervising.

question: The report is concise, accurate and ___.
solution: Adjectival coordination requires a parallel adjective phrase.

question: The programme seeks not only to train staff but also ___ systems.
solution: Not only to train...but also to improve is parallel.

question: I will call you when the meeting ___.
solution: A future time clause introduced by when normally uses the present simple.

question: The proposal, which was submitted yesterday, ___ several revisions.
solution: The subject proposal is singular, so requires is correct.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Although he was tired, but he continued working.
Although he was tired, he continued working.
Although tired, but he continued working.
Although he tired, but continued working.
solution: Although already introduces the contrast, so but is unnecessary.

question: The reason ___ the project was delayed was lack of funding.
solution: The standard construction is the reason why something happened.

question: Choose the correctly placed modifier.
options: Walking to work, the rain soaked Maya.
Walking to work, Maya was soaked by the rain.
The rain, walking to work, soaked Maya.
Maya, the rain walking to work, was soaked.
solution: Maya is the person walking to work, so the introductory modifier correctly refers to Maya.

question: Choose the clearest sentence.
options: The officer reviewed the file carefully that contained errors.
The officer carefully reviewed the file that contained errors.
The officer reviewed carefully the file contained errors.
The officer the file reviewed carefully that contained errors.
solution: The modifier carefully is naturally placed before the verb phrase, and the relative clause clearly modifies file.

question: If I ___ more time, I would revise the report.
solution: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause.

question: If she had studied harder, she ___ the examination.
solution: The third conditional uses would have plus past participle.

question: Unless you ___ the form, your application cannot be processed.
solution: Unless introduces a real condition, so present simple is used for the future meaning.

question: Had the warning been issued earlier, the accident ___.
solution: Had the warning... is an inverted third conditional, requiring might have been prevented.

question: The committee decided to ___ the proposal until more evidence was available.
solution: Put off means postpone.

question: The new evidence ___ his earlier statement.
solution: Bear out means confirm or support a statement.

question: The manager asked the team to ___ the issue before making a decision.
solution: Look into means investigate.

question: The chairperson called ___ the meeting because several members were absent.
solution: Call off means cancel.

question: When the director arrived, the staff ___ for two hours.
solution: An action continuing before another past event takes past perfect continuous.

question: She said that she ___ the document the following day.
solution: In reported speech, will normally shifts to would when the reporting verb is past.

question: The teacher said, 'I am checking the papers.' Choose the correct reported form.
options: The teacher said that I am checking the papers.
The teacher said that she was checking the papers.
The teacher said that she is checking the papers tomorrow.
The teacher said that she had checked the papers.
solution: Present continuous normally shifts to past continuous in reported speech.

question: He said, 'I finished the work yesterday.' Choose the best reported form.
options: He said that he finished the work yesterday.
He said that he had finished the work the previous day.
He said that he has finished the work tomorrow.
He said that I had finished the work.
solution: Past simple commonly shifts to past perfect and yesterday to the previous day.

question: Choose the passive form: 'The committee approved the plan.'
options: The plan was approved by the committee.
The plan is approved the committee.
The committee was approved by the plan.
solution: The object becomes the passive subject: The plan was approved by the committee.

question: Choose the active form: 'The report was prepared by the analyst.'
options: The analyst was preparing by the report.
The analyst has prepare the report.
solution: The agent analyst becomes the active subject.

question: Choose the best transformation: 'Despite being tired, she continued working.'
options: Although she was tired, she continued working.
Although she tired, but she continued working.
Because she was tired, she stopped working.
She continued working because she was tired.
solution: Despite being tired can be expressed as Although she was tired.

question: Choose the sentence closest in meaning: 'As soon as the bell rang, the students left.'
options: The students left long before the bell rang.
No sooner had the bell rung than the students left.
The students left although the bell never rang.
The students waited until after the bell rang.
solution: No sooner had...than expresses an immediate sequence.

question: Which sentence is grammatically correct in standard formal English?
options: Everyone has submitted his or her form.
solution: Everyone is grammatically singular in traditional formal agreement.

question: Choose the most formal sentence.
options: The data shows that the policy ain't working.
The data indicate that the policy is ineffective.
The data is showing the policy ain't effective.
The data indicates that the policy don't work.
solution: The option uses formal vocabulary and standard agreement.

question: The officer is responsible ___ preparing the report.
solution: The standard collocation is responsible for.

question: She is interested ___ public administration.
solution: Interested takes the preposition in.

question: The decision was made ___ accordance with the law.
solution: The fixed expression is in accordance with.

question: The proposal is expensive; ___, it may produce substantial long-term savings.
solution: However introduces a contrast between cost and long-term benefit.

question: In the sentence 'The extremely careful officer checked the file,' the word 'extremely' is a
solution: Extremely modifies the adjective careful, so it is an adverb.

question: In 'The committee approved the proposal,' the word 'proposal' is a
solution: Proposal names a thing and functions as the object of approved.

question: In 'The revised policy was remarkably effective,' 'revised' functions as a
solution: Revised modifies policy and functions adjectivally in the noun phrase.

question: Neither the reports nor the final recommendation ___ convincing.
solution: The nearer subject recommendation is singular, so is is correct.

question: There ___ several reasons for the delay.
solution: The real subject reasons is plural, so are is required.

question: I ___ this book twice, but I still find it useful.
solution: The present perfect describes an experience up to the present.

question: By 2030, the agency ___ the digital system for several years.
solution: An action continuing up to a future point takes future perfect continuous.

question: The training focused on identifying risks, assessing impacts and ___ solutions.
solution: The gerund sequence identifying, assessing, designing is parallel.

question: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The officer ___ prepared the report received an award.'
solution: Who refers to a person functioning as the subject of prepared.

question: Choose the correct form: 'The department ___ budget was reduced requested an explanation.'
solution: Whose expresses possession: the department's budget.

question: Choose the sentence without a dangling modifier.
options: After reviewing the file, the error became obvious.
After reviewing the file, the officer noticed the error.
After reviewing the file, the error was noticed.
After reviewing, the file showed the error.
solution: The officer is the person who reviewed the file, so the modifier is correctly attached.

question: If the data ___ more reliable, the conclusion would be stronger.
solution: This hypothetical present condition uses were in the if-clause.

question: The minister asked officials to ___ the matter urgently.
solution: Deal with means handle or address.

question: She said, 'I can complete it today.' Choose the best reported form.
options: She said that she can complete it today.
She said that she could complete it that day.
She said that I could complete it today.
She said that she had completed it that day.
solution: Can shifts to could and today shifts to that day in standard reported speech.

question: Choose the best transformation: 'It is believed that the policy will succeed.'
options: The policy is believed to succeed.
The policy is believing to succeed.
solution: The impersonal passive can be transformed using subject plus be believed plus infinitive.

question: The report consists ___ five sections.
solution: The fixed construction is consists of.

question: ___ the evidence was limited, the committee reached a cautious conclusion.
solution: Although introduces a subordinate concessive clause.

question: In 'They worked efficiently,' the word 'efficiently' is a
solution: Efficiently modifies the verb worked, so it is an adverb.

question: More than one employee ___ complained about the delay.
solution: More than one normally takes a singular verb.

question: She usually ___ to work by bus, but today she is walking.
solution: The present simple describes a habitual action.

question: The policy is intended to increase access, reduce inequality and ___ accountability.
solution: The infinitive-like coordination uses increase, reduce, strengthen.

question: If it rains tomorrow, the event ___ indoors.
solution: The first conditional uses present simple in the if-clause and will in the main clause.

question: Choose the best transformation: 'No other applicant was as qualified as Maya.'
options: Maya was the most qualified applicant.
Maya was less qualified than every applicant.
Every applicant was more qualified than Maya.
solution: The superlative expresses the same comparison.

question: The meeting starts ___ 10 a.m. ___ Monday.
solution: At is used for clock time and on for a particular day.

question: Choose the clearest sentence.
options: Using the new software, the report was completed quickly by the officer.
Using the new software, the officer completed the report quickly.
The report, using the new software, completed the officer quickly.
The officer completed using the new software the report quickly.
solution: The officer is the user of the software, so the modifier correctly refers to the subject.

question: In 'The proposal was approved unanimously,' the word 'unanimously' is a
solution: Unanimously modifies the verb phrase was approved.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What the committee needs are clearer rules.
What the committee needs is clearer rules.
What the committee needs is clearer guidance.
What the committee need are clearer guidance.
solution: The subject What the committee needs is treated as singular, and clearer guidance is an appropriate singular/uncountable complement.

question: The evidence was incomplete; ___, the committee postponed its decision.
solution: Therefore expresses the result: because the evidence was incomplete, the decision was postponed.
